title: Auraland Art presents group exhibition 'Samsara' at Somers Gallery in London
summary: From 4 to 10 August 2026, Auraland Art , an independent international arts organisation, presented Samsara, a contemporary group exhibition at Somers Gallery in London. Bringing together 23 artists from diverse creative backgrounds, the exhibition explored the cyclical nature of life, the passage of time, and the processes of disruption, transformation, and reconstruction through a range of contemporary visual art practices. The exhibition took its title from Samsara, a Sanskrit term referring to the continuous cycle of existence, death, and rebirth. Rather than approaching cycles as mere repetition, Samsara considered them as ongoing processes of change, in which established structures are continually disrupted, reconfigured, and renewed. title: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston hosts major Winslow Homer watercolor retrospective
summary: Few American artists are as closely associated with the outdoors as Winslow Homer (1836–1910), and few rival his ability to depict it in watercolor. This fall, visitors to the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to see the largest collection in the world of Homer's watercolors, from the holdings of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. Because of the works' sensitivity to light, they have not been displayed together in almost half a century. The exhibition, Of Light and Air: Winslow Homer from the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, is on view at the MFAH from November 1, 2026, through February 7, 2027. The MFAH is the only travel venue for the show, which was organized by and debuted at the MFA Boston in fall 2025. title: Cristin Tierney Gallery presents Maureen O'Leary's solo exhibition 'The Linden Trees'
summary: Cristin Tierney Gallery is presenting The Linden Trees, a solo exhibition of recent paintings and writings by Maureen O’Leary. This is the artist's second solo show with the gallery. The exhibition will be on view through Saturday, December 19th. Coinciding with the exhibition, the artist will release an animated film and a publication with the same title. The gallery will also present new paintings by O’Leary at the ADAA Fair from November 12th through 16th. The Linden Trees is O’Leary’s first narrative painting installation. Composed of thirty-four oil paintings and thirty-five text panels written by the artist, the work gives new life to two female characters from 19th-century Russian literature: Natasha Rostova from Leo Tolstoy's War and Peace and Princess Polina from Alexander Pushkin's unfinished story Roslavlev. O’Leary reimagines what might have been possible for these women had their artistic ambitions

title: The definitive book on Korean abstract art and its aesthetic influence and cultural legacy
summary: Phaidon presents Dansaekhwa: Korean Abstract Art and its Cultural Impact , a major new study of the groundbreaking postwar movement that redefined Korean abstract art. Written by leading art historian Dr. Yeon Shim Chung, this beautifully illustrated volume explores the aesthetic legacy and cultural influence of Dansaekhwa, revealing how a generation of Korean artists radically expanded the possibilities of painting through process, tactility, and experimentation. Although Dansaekhwa is often translated simply as "monochrome painting," it extends far beyond the canvas into drawing, sculpture, installation, conceptual art, and experimental work. Emerging in South Korea during the 1970s, artists developed new visual languages rooted in repetitive processes, tactile surfaces, and the exploration of material, transforming painting into a deeply physical and meditative experience. title: Kunsthalle Bremen opens first major art exhibition dedicated to the dachshund
summary: "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" (31 October 2026 – 28 March 2027) is the first exhibition dedicated to dachshunds in art. With around 120 historical and contemporary works, the show explores various perspectives of the dachshund in art, ranging from its origin as a hunting dog, its role as an urban companion of the bourgeoisie, popular muse and inspiration to artists through to the iconic figure we find everywhere today. In addition, dachshunds themselves will be both protagonists and audience during the exhibition. With major works, the show "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" traces the appearance of the dachshund in art, starting with its traditional role as hunting dog, its popularity as companions of the bourgeoisie and today its emergence as ubiquitous iconic and fashionable figure. title: Taichung Art Museum to present SANAA's largest exhibition to date, Architecture & Environment
summary: Taichung Art Museum will present Kazuyo Sejima + Ryue Nishizawa / SANAA Architecture & Environment, on view from January 30 to May 9 2027, at the Taichung Green Museumbrary. Founded by internationally acclaimed architects Kazuyo Sejima and Ryue Nishizawa, SANAA presents its largest exhibition to date. The show brings together architectural drawings, models, photography, and archival materials spanning three decades of design practice. Featuring projects across different periods, geographical contexts, and scales, the exhibition highlights the work of SANAA, Kazuyo Sejima & Associates, and the Office of Ryue Nishizawa. An extensive collection of architectural models offers rare insights into the design process, inviting visitors to explore SANAA’ s architectural aesthetic from multiple perspectives. title: Yayoi Kusama infinity mirror room headlines major group exhibition at OGR Torino
summary: From October 31, 2026 to February 25, 2027, OGR Torino, the hub of Fondazione CRT, presents The Quantum Effect, a major exhibition exploring the impact of quantum theory on visual culture—cinema, popular culture and contemporary art. Curated by Daniel Birnbaum and Jacqui Davies, the project unfolds through a group exhibition examining the paradoxes of space and time through the work of some of the most influential artists on the international scene, Cerith Wyn Evans, Isa Genzken, Tomás Saraceno, Mark Leckey, Rirkrit Tiravanija, Sturtevant and Man Ray, among others. Produced by OGR Torino and SMAC Venice (San Marco Art Centre), the exhibition is accompanied by an ambitious programme of related initiatives. Highlights include the presentation of an infinity mirror room by Yayoi Kusama. title: Six artists examine suspended time and non-linear narratives at Galerie Urs Meile
summary: Galerie Urs Meile Beijing is presenting Time Out of Joint, a group exhibition featuring six artists who have been in ongoing dialogue with the gallery over the past few years. These conversations and reflections are condensed into the exhibition. Using excavation as a metaphor for time, the exhibition explores a suspended state in which linear chronology breaks down and past, present, and future overlap. Familiar frames of reference are beginning to shift, but a new order has yet to emerge. Following three pairs of parallel, interconnected paths, the six artists converge on this unsettled present. Drawing on classical traditions, Wendi Yan and Zhou Jiangnan rework materials from the past to tell stories about the present. title: MACTE - Museo di Arte Contemporanea di Termoli appoints Rossella Farinotti as Artistic Director
summary: MACTE—Museo di Arte Contemporanea di Termoli announces the appointment of Rossella Farinotti as its new Artistic Director, effective December 1, 2026. Her programme will be announced following her arrival, with the first exhibition scheduled for February 2027. Located in Termoli, in Italy's Molise region, MACTE promotes contemporary art and culture and cares for the collection of the Premio Termoli. Farinotti's practice brings together contemporary art, public space and community engagement, connecting curatorial research with the places and people through which it develops. Farinotti was directly appointed by the Board of Directors and President Paolo De Matteis Larivera following a process initiated last spring. The Board recognised in her experience the expertise and vision needed to guide the Museum through its next phase of development. She succeeds Caterina Riva, who has led MACTE since September 2020. title: Morgan Library & Museum presents Swedish Neoclassicist Johan Tobias Sergel
summary: Johan Tobias Sergel (1740–1814) is one of Sweden's most important artists and a leading figure of European Neoclassicism, yet he remains relatively unknown outside Sweden. Internationally celebrated during his lifetime, and heralded by some as the greatest sculptor since antiquity, he later faded from the broader narrative of European art history. This fall, the Morgan Library & Museum introduces him to a new generation of audiences with Fantasy and Reality: The Art of Johan Tobias Sergel, the first major exhibition devoted to the artist outside Europe. On view October 30, 2026, through January 31, 2027, the exhibition brings together a significant selection of Sergel's works, including sculpture in terracotta, marble, bronze, and plaster, and a major group of the artist's drawings, which reveal his great humanity and keen eye for the complexities of human nature. title: Posthumous Joyce Pensato exhibition brings pop-abstract works to Hamburg
summary: With her bold, gestural painting style, New York artist Joyce Pensato became the icon of the fusion of American pop culture and Abstract Expressionism. Mickey, Donald, Batman, The Simpsons, and South Park—through Pensato’s subversive appropriation, these familiar comic and cartoon characters reveal a darker, often unsettling yet deeply affecting side. EYES FOR YOU is the first major solo exhibition in Europe dedicated to the artist since her death in 2019. The exhibition traces the development of Joyce Pensato’s work, from her early still lifes and Batman drawings of the 1970s to the large-scale black-and-white enamel paintings of the 1990s, in which the New York artist brought drawing and painting together for the first time. title: Zhang Yunyao explores graphite on felt in new exhibition at White Cube
summary: Zhang Yunyao’s exhibition ‘When the Surface Thinks’ comprises a suite of graphite drawings on felt, executed with near-photographic precision. A response to philosopher Paul Valéry’s ironic quip that ‘what is deepest in man is the skin – insofar as he knows himself’, Zhang’s work at once tests the limits of representation and demonstrates his mastery of his medium.1 Now based in Paris, Zhang graduated in 2007 from the College of Fine Arts at Shanghai Normal University in China, before moving to Europe in 2020. Subverting the traditions of Soviet Realism and the French Beaux-Arts in which he was trained, Zhang brings together depictions of classical statuary, ancient masks and illusionistic structures from engineering plans and medical science. Through techniques of tight cropping or mirroring, Zhang creates abstract yet eerily faithful renderings that exploit aesthetic ideals such as symmetry, true likeness and compositional balance. title: Antonio Canova's unrealized monument to Horatio Nelson explored in new exhibition in Italy
summary: The Museo Gypsotheca Antonio Canova in Possagno is presenting "A Grand and Immortal Work: Antonio Canova's Monument to Horatio Nelson," an exhibition exploring the celebrated Italian sculptor's ambitious but ultimately unrealized funerary monument dedicated to one of Britain's greatest naval heroes. On view from November 1, 2026, through April 25, 2027, the exhibition brings together drawings, plaster models, paintings, and delicate wax reliefs that illuminate Canova's creative process and his interpretation of heroism in the modern age. Curated by Paolo Mariuz, the exhibition offers a detailed examination of the project Canova developed between 1806 and 1808 to commemorate Admiral Horatio Nelson (1758–1805), the Royal Navy commander whose victory at the Battle of Trafalgar secured his place among Britain's most celebrated national

title: Cleveland Museum of Art and The Jewish Museum partner for major ritual art installation
summary: The Cleveland Museum of Art (CMA), in partnership with the Jewish Museum, New York, presents Furnishing American Synagogues: Jewish Ceremonial Art, a new installation of Jewish ritual objects on view in two of the museum’s permanent collection galleries from November 1, 2026, through October 24, 2027. In observance of the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, these loans feature Jewish ritual objects used in synagogues and daily life in the United States since its founding. The works range from an early 1900s silver Torah crown, or an adornment for a closed Torah scroll, to contemporary mixed-media works such as an alms (donation) container. title: Museum de Fundatie launches international search for contemporary art curator to help shape its future
summary: Museum de Fundatie, one of the Netherlands' leading art museums, has announced a search for a curator of contemporary art to help shape its exhibitions, research, and public programming. The full-time position, based across the museum's locations in Zwolle and Heino, offers an opportunity to work with a collection spanning more than five centuries while introducing new international perspectives and engaging diverse audiences. The museum is seeking an experienced curator with an inquiring mind, broad art-historical knowledge, and a strong understanding of contemporary artistic practices beyond Europe and the United States. The successful candidate will help develop exhibitions and publications, strengthen relationships with artists and researchers, and explore new ways of connecting the institution's collection with contemporary

title: Vadim Fishkin wins the first edition of the award promoted by Seletti at Artissima 2026
summary: Vadim Fishkin, presented by Galleria Gregor Podnar in the Back to the Future section, is the winner of the first edition of the Seletti Wonder Award, a new prize established through a collaboration between Seletti and Artissima, the international contemporary art fair taking place in Turin until 1 November. In line with the company’s commitment to supporting artistic research and experimentation, the award aims to identify an artist whose work offers an original perspective on reality, through a language that reflects Seletti’s attitude towards what is transcultural, innovative and provocative, while remaining direct, accessible and communicative. Vadim Fishkin (born in 1965 in Russia, lives and works in Ljubljana) was selected by a jury comprising artists Eva and Franco Mattes, Ilenia Paneghini, President of RETI Spa and a collector, radio presenter

title: Zander Galerie announces representation of Mexican artist duo Lake Verea
summary: Zander Galerie announced the representation of Mexican artist duo Lake Verea, Francisca Rivero-Lake Cortina (b. 1973) and Carla Verea Hernández (b. 1978), both born in Mexico City. The announcement follows their first exhibition in the Cologne gallery, presented this summer, marking the beginning of a new collaboration and an ongoing commitment to the duo’s distinctive photographic practice. For more than two decades, Lake Verea has approached some of the most celebrated examples of twentieth-century architecture from an unexpected perspective: at daylight and nightlight, illuminated by the full moon and transformed through playful interventions. title: David Peter Francis presents group exhibition 'Rainbow Room'
summary: David Peter Francis presents Rainbow Room, a group exhibition presenting new and recent works by Sophie Kovel, Heji Shin, Ronald Sterling, and Kianja Strobert. Rainbow Room is the epitome of New York glamour, where iconic skyline views, world-class dining, and impeccable service create unforgettable events. From star-studded celebrations to elegant gatherings, this legendary venue has hosted presidents, dignitaries, and entertainment icons — now, it's your turn. Both in imaging the orchids on the grounds of Marjorie Merriweather Post's Hillwood Estate and the paths lining the perimeter of Mark Zuckerberg's property, Sophie Kovel's works in the exhibition pinpoint succinct nuclei of concentrated wealth, cataloging the inextricable ties between power and aesthetic infrastructures. title: Kunst Halle Sankt Gallen announces regional survey ahead of major December refurbishment
summary: The time is fast approaching: In December 2026, the refurbishing works will begin on the New Foyer of the Kunst Halle Sankt Gallen, which will become a space for meetings and events – not only for the Kunst Halle itself, but also for an expanded network of partners, associations and creatives. The grand re-opening will take place in spring 2027. The Kunst Halle Sankt Gallen wishes to use this significant moment to celebrate its artistic community and the values of togetherness, solidarity and friendship which – through all the changes – define it as an exhibition venue and institution. title: Piero Gilardi's socially engaged practices and agitprop works surveyed at PAV Torino
summary: PAV – Parco Arte Vivente presents From art to life, an exhibition curated by Marco Scotini and dedicated to a pivotal period in the career of Piero Gilardi (Turin, 1942–2023), marked by his withdrawal from the conventional art system and his engagement with social movements. The exhibition is the second instalment in a series of monographic exhibitions devoted by PAV to its founding artist, following Car Crash. Piero Gilardi and Arte Povera (2023). While the first exhibition explored Gilardi’s early work and his initial relationship with the Arte Povera movement in the 1960s, From Art to Life traces a trajectory that begins in the 1970s and 1980s and extends to works produced in the 2000s, documenting the decisive shift away from object-based art towards radical forms of social engagement, collective care and political emancipation. title: Jameel Arts Centre presents Salah Elmur: Just as the Heart of a Mango is a Stone
summary: Art Jameel, an organisation that supports artists and creative communities, presents Salah Elmur: Just as the Heart of a Mango is a Stone, a major solo exhibition at Jameel Arts Centre, Dubai's hub for contemporary art and ideas. On view from November 1 2026 to March 14 2027 in Galleries 4-8 on the museum’s First Floor, the exhibition will be preceded by a public preview on October 31, from 5:00pm to 8:00pm, featuring a conversation on Elmur's practice led by Melissa Gronlund and a performance by musician Asim Eltayeb Gurashi. Bringing together paintings, archival photographs, sketches and ephemera spanning the last decade of Elmur's practice, alongside loans from major regional and international collections, including the Sharjah Art Foundation Collection and the Saudi Museum of Contemporary Art (SAMoCA), the exhibition offers

title: Heidi Lau unveils largest suspended ceramic installation to date in New York exhibition
summary: Sikkema Malloy Jenkins is presenting Ouroboros, an installation of ceramic sculptural work by artist Heidi Lau. On view from October 30 through December 19, 2026, Ouroboros expands upon Pavilion Procession, a major installation by Lau shown in the Sigg Prize 2025 Exhibition at M+ in Hong Kong. The title of the exhibition, Ouroboros, refers to an ancient totem of a snake or dragon in a circular formation swallowing its own tail. Interpreted as a reference to the cyclical nature of life, death and rebirth, for Lau it also points to a blurred distinction between phenomena and beings. Through hand-built, textured ceramics, Heidi Lau creates ritual objects, funerary monuments, fossilized creatures, and miniature universes.
